messages.author: 29468662cf83e2ce
messages.subject: Converged replications
parts:
Dear all,

I am simulating data by Monte Carlo using the simsem() function to understand how the growth model behaves in certain scenarios. The number of converged replications is very low in some of the scenarios.
I  would like to know if the average of the parameter estimates and SE are calculated using the results of all replications (including the nonconvergent replications), or only those of the convergent replications. For instance, averages of the simulation results regarding the information below, are calculated considering a total of 1000 replications or a total of 518 replications?

Number of replications = 1000
Number of converged replications = 518
Number of nonconverged replications:
   1. Nonconvergent Results = 0
   2. Nonconvergent results from multiple imputation = 0
   3. At least one SE were negative or NA = 0
   4. At least one variance estimates were negative = 59
   5. At least one correlation estimates were greater than 1 or less than -1 = 0
   6. Model-implied covariance matrices of any groups of latent variables are not positive definite = 423


I really appreciate your help! Thank you!
Best
Catarina

messages.author: 5d4f9e7f97c21008
messages.subject: Re: Converged replications
parts:
Hi Catarina,

By default summary will only provide results from converged replications with proper solutions (so 518 replications in your case). To get a summary for all replications use the summaryParam function to summarize results and set improper = FALSE as an argument.

Alex
